STATUS 2026-11-03 (verified against develop): the code work below has landed. benchbox compare has --min-aggregate-regression-delta (benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py), both .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml and .github/workflows/perf-smoke.yml pass --min-aggregate-regression-delta 82ms, and docs/internal/perf-smoke.md says the workflow runs on pull requests to the release branch (PR #2859; the page moved from docs/development in #2817). What remains is the closing decision below. This item still carries a need on t3-perf-execution-variants-regression-20261010 because its verification dispatch (run 38027036252) failed at 640 ms versus 547 ms and the hosted cause is unresolved; a later nightly (39125986956) was not red.

DECISION GATE (owner): close this item on the landed evidence and drop the need edge, or keep waiting for the 640 ms investigation. Agent prepares the brief; only the owner decides; do not remove the need edge without the owner's quoted words.
Brief must list, from live reads (gh run list/view for nightly-v2, read-only): the t3:perf outcome and total execution time of each of the last 14 nightly-v2 runs with run ids; which, if any, failed above both the 10% threshold and the 82 ms floor; and the runner CPU class of each.

Original text follows.

Decision (owner, 2026-10-09): option (c). The aggregate check (Total Execution Time and Average Query Time) fails only when the aggregate is both more than the percentage threshold slower and more than an absolute number of milliseconds slower. Keep the 10% threshold and the per-query gate (10% and 7 ms) unchanged.

Work:
- Add an aggregate floor to `benchbox compare` (benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py; today --min-regression-delta applies to per-query checks only, compare.py:284 "Aggregate metrics are judged by percentage alone"), for example `--min-aggregate-regression-delta`.
- Derive the floor from the same-runner-class spread and record the method next to the baseline (docs/internal/perf-smoke.md). Same-class totals so far: 539.8, 542.9, 546.4, 548.9, 586.1 and 604.7 ms, a spread of about 65 ms.
- Pass the floor in nightly-v2.yml (lines 213-214) and perf-smoke.yml (lines 59-60).

Options considered and not chosen: keep 10% alone (red most nights); raise to 15% (as arbitrary as 10% with six samples); report-only aggregates (loses the uniform-slowdown signal); rolling same-class history or two consecutive red nights (more machinery, delays signal); larger scale factor or more iterations (more runner time). Revisit (e) if the floor still fails on noise once more same-class samples exist.

Evidence:
- The aggregate is the sum of the same 66 per-query timings (22 queries x 3 iterations, about 8 ms each) that the per-query check judges.
- In run 37991400931 all 22 queries slowed together (+2.7% to +45.8%) on the baseline's own runner class (AMD EPYC 7763): host noise, not a code regression.
- The gate does not measure orchestration overhead: run.total_duration_ms is not compared.
- perf-smoke.yml runs only on pull requests to the release branch (perf-smoke.yml:3-5), so the "Per-PR" title and wording in docs/internal/perf-smoke.md are wrong.
- t3:perf failed in 11 of the last 12 nightly-v2 runs.
